en: Points of Controversy The Chapter on the Path of Certainty The Sixth Section
The Discourse on the Fixed Course: Is the fixed course unconditioned? Yes.
“Is Nibbāna a refuge, a shelter, a resort, a final goal, the undecaying, the deathless?
“One should not say so…” [and so on].
“Is the fixed course (niyāma) unconditioned? Is Nibbāna unconditioned?”
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are there two unconditioned phenomena?
One should not speak thus … [as before] … .
"Are there two unconditioned things?
"Yes.
"Are they two refuges, two shelters, two resorts, two final goals, two states of immortality, two deathless states, two nibbānas?"
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “Are there two Nibbānas? Yes.
Is there a state of high and low, inferior and superior, excellence and deficiency, a boundary, a division, a line, or an interval between the two kinds of *nibbāna*?
One should not say so… [as before]… Is the fixed course (*niyāma*) unconditioned (*asaṅkhata*)?
“Yes.

“Is it the case that there are some who enter into the fixed course of rightness (niyāma), obtain it, produce it, cause it to arise, bring it forth, cause it to arise together, generate it, cause it to be generated, engender it, and cause it to be engendered?
“Yes.”

Is it the case that some enter into the unconditioned, obtain it, produce it, cause it to arise, cause it to emerge, cause it to manifest, cause it to be fully manifested, generate it, or cause it to be fully generated?
It should not be said so... [etc. ...
Is the fixed course (niyāma) unconditioned?
“Yes,” you say.
“Then is the Path unconditioned?
You should not say so … [as before] … .
Is the path conditioned?
Yes. Is the fixed course (niyāma) conditioned? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the certainty of stream-entry unconditioned? Yes.
Is the path of stream-entry unconditioned?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is the path of stream-entry conditioned?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is the certainty of stream-entry conditioned?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
Is the certainty of once-returning …pe… the certainty of non-returning …pe… the certainty of arahantship unconditioned?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is the path of arahantship unconditioned?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
Is the path to arahantship conditioned?
Yes. Is the certainty of arahantship conditioned?
It should not be said so... [etc.
...Is the certainty of stream-entry unconditioned?
...Is the certainty of arahantship unconditioned? Is Nibbāna unconditioned?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are there five unconditioned things?
You should not say so …pe…
"Are there five unconditioned things?
"Yes. "Are there five refuges... [and so on]...
Does the intermediate space blow?
One should not say so… [as before]… Is the fixed course (niyāma) unconditioned (asaṅkhata)?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is the fixed course of wrongness unconditioned?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is the fixed course of wrongness conditioned?
Yes. Is the fixed course of rightness conditioned? Yes.
It should not be said so ... [as before] ...
Should it not be said that "the fixed course (niyāma) is unconditioned (asaṅkhata)"?
“Yes.
“When what has arisen and ceased in the fixed course (niyāma) becomes unfixed (aniyata), is that so?
“One should not say so…” [and so forth].
"In that case, the fixed course (niyāma) must be unconditioned (asaṅkhata).
[If so,] when one has arisen and ceased in the fixed course of wrongness (micchattaniyāma), would it not follow that one is in the unfixed state (aniyata)?
One should not say this... [and so on]."
Therefore, the fixed course of wrongness is unconditioned.
The Discussion on the Fixed Course is finished.
